_purpose: Orchestrator continuity across Claude Code sessions. The HUMAN talks to ONE AI (the orchestrator); that AI dispatches scope-specific work via the Agent tool. When the human starts a fresh Claude Code session, the new orchestrator MUST read this file early in startup so it knows: what was last being worked on, what's pending, what decisions were just made, what scopes are currently claimed, what to NOT re-do.
_protocol: Update this file at every significant decision/checkpoint. Treat it like a running session journal — newest at the bottom of recent_decisions, oldest pruned. The aggregator script `node scripts/agent-status.js` complements this with per-scope status from data/coordination/sessions/*.json.
_what_vs_why: As of v0.283.x: this file records WHY decisions were made (running journal). `docs/PRIORITIES.md` records WHAT comes next (strict-ranked backlog). Both must be updated when scope changes. Don't put 'next action' here — put it in PRIORITIES.md.

recent_decisions.decision: Step D (reports the admins can check, design 10e) merged from three parallel worktrees, released as v0.1469.0: report_v2 signed by the reporter over a pinned preimage with a BLAKE3 evidence hash; DM evidence checked by the relay against the target signature over the DM v2 inner words; posts looked up; group text unproven; Reports for admins and mods (mods never see the reporter); decisions through the moderation rules; 90-day cull after decision. Also the outside-help findings (18 countries, dated, quoted), the desktop built-in copy of report_reasons.json, and moderators spelled either way see Reports.
recent_decisions.why: The operator: protect the users. A web builder noticed a DM carrying an encrypted file holds its key in the text; a report could hand an admin the means to open abuse imagery, which is itself a crime to view or pass on. Since the signature covers the text, such messages can never be evidence: refused by the relay and offered by neither client (marker matched in any version). The underlying legal duties of a server operator on such a report are logged in PRIORITIES for a dated findings document.

recent_decisions.decision: Step B (who can reach me, design 10c) merged from three parallel worktrees: relay (reach_settings table, reach_set/reach_settings/reach_refused, enforcement at dm_put, voice_call and its signals, trade_request and dc_offer, the groups audience, open calls tracked in memory as a hash of the two keys, contact requests 5 a day), desktop (Settings > Safety, People who may call me re-issuing passes, refusal notice, Requests list), web (the mirror, plus window.peerData exposed so names resolve). Safe defaults: messages friends, calls chosen, trades friends; admins bound.
recent_decisions.why: The operator: safe by default, choose individuals for calls. The web build found the first contact-request design could never form a friendship under the defaults and could be spoofed (256 bytes cannot hold a signature); amended mid-build so a request is an ordinary signed sealed DM carrying the requester s pass, and the accepter s reply attaches it, keeping the relay free of who-asked-whom records. The relay build found the 256-byte rule could never have worked anyway (every signed DM pads to 16,384).

recent_decisions.decision: Released v0.1466.0: friendship passes v2 (design 10b step A): hum/friend/v2 preimage with the server DID, a random serial and a may list (call, invite, message, trade, voice_message; new friends get all but call), no end date; withdrawal by cert_revoke into friend_cert_revocations stored under a keyed BLAKE3 fingerprint (the erased-accounts secret, domain hum/withdrawn-pass/v1) and kept past an account erase; the pass rides on dm_put, trade_request, voice_call, dc_offer and profile requests; may is read but not yet enforced (step B).
recent_decisions.why: The operator: friendships must never expire (parents and brothers), and consent must be revocable (the Accord). Reviewed the relay check before merging and sent the branch back once for the fingerprint and keep-past-erase changes. Accepted risk: withdrawal rows are permanent and bounded at 4,096 per key; a throwaway key could add about 400 KB, less than one day of the 20 knocks a key may already deposit. Found while building: the web Trade page never signs in (logged in PRIORITIES).

recent_decisions.decision: Operator answers on the safety design (docs/design/blocking-and-safe-mode.md section 10a): SAFE BY DEFAULT, with a per-kind "Who can reach me" table (messages, voice messages, calls, invitations, trades; audiences nobody / people I choose in named lists / friends / my groups / anyone); calls default to people I choose; strangers can send a name-only contact request. Friendships never expire (no end date; withdrawal by serial). Our own STUN responder plus a room-scoped forwarder on one UDP port, Google removed, calls through the server by default, direct opt-in, WebSocket fallback; MMO public voice server-routed by proximity. Each federated server runs its own; cross-server calls go server to server. Other recommendations accepted (blocked not told, friends-only binds admins, Protected setup name, reports 90 days).
recent_decisions.why: Operator, verbatim in 10a. Raised for a later identity-on-every-device design: hardware security keys (as an unlock factor via the FIDO2 hmac-secret feature, since the keys sign with classical, not post-quantum, algorithms), sign-in on a new device by scanning a standard QR code carrying our own prefix from a device already signed in, NFC security keys, and per-device keys certified by the identity so a lost device can be cut off without changing who you are.

recent_decisions.decision: Step E (our own STUN and the room-scoped call forwarder, design 10f) merged from three parallel worktrees, released as v0.1470.0: one UDP port with a rate-limited STUN responder and a closed TURN forwarder whose relayed addresses are virtual and which delivers only between allocations of the same room; call_credentials over the signed-in socket; both clients connect calls and rooms relay only, Google removed everywhere (a native lint scans src, web and app/web), group mesh and contact channels off, direct offers answered only from own devices.
recent_decisions.why: The operator approved it (Do we have to go through Google? and Let us do this). The forwarder cannot reach any outside address, which is what made the 2026-08-07 reflector possible. Calls stay unavailable, said plainly, until the operator opens UDP 3478 with the command in docs/admin/call-forwarder.md; the AI does not change firewall settings.

recent_decisions.decision: Step F (warnings and the recovery-phrase guard, design 10g) merged from two parallel worktrees (web chat, desktop app), released as v0.1471.0: warnings under direct and group messages matched from data/safety/warnings.json by one normalising rule on both clients (Unicode \p{Alphabetic}\p{N} on web equals Rust char::is_alphanumeric, 17 shared cases in scripts/tests/fixtures/warning-cases.json), a stranger's links held until Open, and a send holding 4 or more of the sender's own recovery-phrase words in a row stopped with no send-anyway. Number-only words are now left out before the run check, so a phrase pasted as a numbered list is stopped too (found by the desktop agent). Reported posts show admins neither a file nor a link (relay without_files_or_links).
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for tools that protect people from scams and predators, for everyone and not only children. Warnings are checked on the device only, because messages are end-to-end encrypted and nobody, admins included, can read them. The numbered-list gap mattered because backup screens show the phrase numbered, which is exactly how people copy it. The admin redaction follows the 2026-10-10 report-duties finding: a reported post must never put abuse material in front of an admin.

recent_decisions.decision: Step B and D follow-ups built on both clients from four parallel worktrees and released as v0.1472.0: 10c-ii, a Message, Call and Trade tick per friend on "People I choose" (the pass carries message+invite+voice_message, trade, call; invite alone when nothing is ticked, because the format refuses an empty may), and 10e-ii, help outside this server in the report dialog (emergency number, also lines, the child-report body, a country the person picks, kept on the device, never sent, https links only). The web halves chose the open wording first and the desktop halves were told to match; the spec records the as-built words and two deliberate desktop differences.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked to choose individuals who may message or call; until 10c-ii "People I choose" only worked for calls. The help lines follow the dated outside-help finding. Building web and desktop against one written spec, then having the second builder match the first one's choices, kept the two apps saying the same words.

recent_decisions.decision: Two dated findings written before the protected setup: children's online-safety rules (COPPA and the FTC Act, US states, UK Children's code and Online Safety Act, EU DSA and GDPR) and California AB 1043 as rewritten by AB 1856 (in force 1 January 2027). Spec 10h (step G, the protected setup) written from them, with every on-screen word in data/gui/safety_presets.json; web and desktop builders dispatched. Three operator decisions recorded in PRIORITIES: the age position (the web chat says 18 or older), content rules on the project server's rules page, and whether to email the FTC COPPA hotline.
recent_decisions.why: CLAUDE.md requires a dated primary-source finding before any "for children" claim. The finding says nothing forbids a parent's PIN lock and nothing supports "kid safe" or "compliant"; the FTC has acted on parental-control claims with gaps (Messenger Kids), so 10h adds a review of existing friends, groups and rooms when the setup is turned on, and an always-visible line telling the person it is on (ICO standard 11). AB 1043 now forbids asking the operating system for an age when not required, so the setup never asks, and a store listing needs a decision first.

recent_decisions.decision: Step G, the protected setup (spec 10h), built on both clients from parallel worktrees and released as v0.1473.0, with every on-screen word in data/gui/safety_presets.json (sentences, lines and 26 labels). Review and alignment after the merge: the web added PIN gates for every copy of the identity (encrypted backup, identity file, device-link code, onboarding phrase step, the settings page); the desktop gained the same gate on its device-link QR; "Forgot the PIN?" got one rule on both apps (a recorded identity must match; a missing or malformed one, which only damage leaves, falls back to the identity in use); a mention in a hidden room no longer dings. BUG-176 found by reading the report dialog's snapshot: v0.1472.0's desktop report dialog hid Send; new widgets::dialog_scrolling.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for a mode that protects kids from predators and scams. The dated finding set the words (never "kid safe" or "compliant") and the shape (review existing contacts, tell the person, no flag sent anywhere). Fail-closed on a damaged identity was rejected because it would lock a damaged setup for good (on the web, clearing site data, identity and all, would be the only way out). BUG-176 shipped because every test passed and nobody read the rendered dialog; the lesson went into BUGS.md and the UI-verification memory.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10i built on the relay and both clients from three parallel worktrees and released as v0.1474.0: an admin or the owner erases another person's data with the person's name typed to confirm. The relay factored the self-erase into one shared function (handlers/account_erase.rs carry_out) both erases call; AccountErased gained by_admin; admin_erase_done carries the receipt; the log names nobody. Moderators cannot erase; admins and the owner cannot be erased this way. The public roadmap also gained the safety work.
recent_decisions.why: The children's online-safety finding (judgement call 7): an operator who learns a member is under 13 is expected to delete the child's information, and only a person could erase their own data. One shared function keeps the admin erase from ever doing less than the self-erase.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10j built (relay, then web first, then desktop matching the web's words; a shared byte-for-byte marker fixture) and released as v0.1475.0 with the step B follow-ups: a report about a P2P group goes to its creator as a flagged sealed DM through one narrow relay exception (both in a group the recipient created, 3 a day); the creator's app checks each item against its own copy; Remove changes the group key first (sealed to everyone but the removed person), on both clients. Also BUG-177 (a busy person's automatic reject told a hidden caller they were online; now it rings out with a missed-call line), a refused contact request marked request:true so neither app offers another, the ten-trade limit no longer counting requests sent to you, and the web Trade page (it never signed in) fixed.
recent_decisions.why: Server admins cannot read or check encrypted group messages, nor remove a member; the creator can. Rekeying on removal is what makes Remove mean anything: without it the removed person keeps reading. The follow-ups were in PRIORITIES from steps B and C; each was small and each closed a real leak or a broken page.

recent_decisions.decision: Released v0.1476.0: spec 10k (files in DMs and P2P groups encrypted on both clients, inline display on the desktop, a marker never sent into a public channel), BUG-178 (Pin, Edit and React refused by the relay outside its own rooms, hidden on private rows, and refused at each send point while a private conversation is open), BUG-179 (the desktop log no longer records file markers, which carried keys), and the account words (terminology_lint gains ACCOUNT_SEED; every "seed" meaning the account key changed to "recovery phrase").
recent_decisions.why: Reviewing the safety follow-ups showed private files only as private as their links: a web DM paste and every group file went up as plain public files. The web 10k build then found its group rows offered the server Pin and Edit, which sent group text in the clear (an admin pin would have been kept and broadcast); the desktop build found DM file keys in run.log. Checked the live server read-only: its only two pins are in #general, so nothing private was ever pinned.

recent_decisions.decision: Batch review of the safety arc (three read-only critics, one feature area each) after v0.1476.0; about 30 seam defects confirmed and fixed in three parallel batches with red-first tests: web shipped as v0.1476.1 together with BUG-180 (v0.1476.0 broke web group rows), relay and desktop as v0.1477.0. Highlights: dm_put gets its own burst bucket (8, then 1/s) and both apps pace pass sweeps; Reply bound to its own conversation; removed group members cannot rejoin with an old ticket, epoch keys cannot be overwritten, newest 200 group messages; reported staff never see their reports; protected setup locks groups, invites and friend codes and lives in its own atomic file. Recorded as BUG-181.
recent_decisions.why: The memory rule feedback_review_after_parallel_waves: systems built side by side disagree at the seams, and every builder had passed its own tests. The review ran after shipping, which let BUG-180 reach the live site for a few hours; next time the critics run before an arc is called done.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10l shipped as v0.1478.0 (relay, web and desktop together, BUG-182): every friendship-pass dm_put carries a random ref; the relay answers dm_put_ok or dm_put_refused {reason} to the sender alone (src/relay/handlers/dm_answer.rs); a pass counts as given only on dm_put_ok, the self-copy waits for it, an unanswered pass is kept as perhaps given (native passes_unanswered, web passesUnsure, at most 4 per friend) and withdrawn with the rest. Exception kept on purpose: an untick (Message, Call or Trade) withdraws the passes allowing it at once, not when the new pass is taken; the friend stays on the People I choose list meanwhile (web passFriends). Same release: a removed group member let back in is sealed to again once a member list asked for after the removal names them; a re-seal ignores members with no Kyber key; the chat limiter no longer subtracts Instants (Windows boot panic); the desktop phrase-lock line draws only its first sentence.
recent_decisions.why: A second review of the batch-review fixes found that pacing only made a refused pass rarer: the relay never said which put it refused, so both apps could show a friendship complete while the friend held no pass. The untick exception follows the earlier rule that consent taken back takes effect now; the desktop builder proposed it and the web took it up with a red-first test. Relay and clients ship together because a client whose ref is never answered records no pass at all.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1479.0 (BUG-183): the web scratch pad treats files like a private conversation (encrypted upload, marker kept in localStorage by app.js scratchPadKeep) and its rows are private rows (SCRATCH_PAD_ROW: no React, Edit, server Pin or Delete); the desktop is_private_channel counts "scratchpad" so its rows offer none either. The PRIORITIES follow-up line about the scratchpad was removed.
recent_decisions.why: The follow-up list said the scratchpad still uploaded plain files; checking both clients showed the desktop had been fixed in v0.1477.0 but the web never was, and neither client hid the row actions that send a row's words to the server. A follow-up list has to be checked against both mirrors, not just the one that was fixed.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1480.0 (BUG-184): each app checks its own "who can reach me" setting for calls on an incoming ring (desktop on_ring via DmStore::admits_from, web ringIgnored), ignoring a refused ring like a blocked caller's; with no store or settings loaded the relay's check stands. The desktop DM screen now counts passes still waiting for an answer (passes_held_by), matching the web's passMayHeld.
recent_decisions.why: Closes the step B follow-up "incoming rings are not also filtered by the callee's own app", the same defence the DM screen already gives against a server that passes something on by mistake. Writing it exposed that the desktop half of 10l had not taught the DM screen about unanswered passes, which the web half had.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1481.0 (BUG-185): the relay stamps each player's identity key beside their name (components.key, and key on game_player_joined); the desktop keeps it on RemotePlayer and skips a blocked key in the figure pass (lib.rs) and nameplate_labels (engine/block.rs hides_player). And components_seen_by_others sends another player only name, appearance and key (PLAYER_FIELDS_SEEN_BY_OTHERS); crew and things keep theirs, a player's own welcome entry keeps all.
recent_decisions.why: Closes the last client-side Block gap (design 4.5, "Game figure and name"). Sending the key was judged no new exposure: the members list already pairs every key with its name. Adding it showed that everyone in view was sent each player's health, inventory, experience and quests, which no client read for anyone else, so that went in the same release. The operator checked in mid-work ("it's been like 12 hours") and was given the status.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10m (docs/design/blocking-and-safe-mode.md, commit bf8c4c582) written from two read-only critic reviews of v0.1478 to v0.1481, and built by a desktop and a web worktree agent in parallel: R1 a contact request follows only on dm_put_ok (desktop); R2 a re-issue that takes something away sends its self-copy at once and the new pass goes out before the withdrawals; R3 a pass withdrawn by my other device marks the friend "changed on my other device" and is never replaced with the defaults; R4 an untick always takes back unanswered passes (desktop); R5 echo guard (desktop); R6 one send per friend and Unfollow drops a waiting send (desktop); R7 a pass refused for reach is not resent on its own; R8 group membership in the apps own DM/ring checks is the relay call; R9 HUD co-presence list skips blocked players; R10 scratch pad: no typing indicator, desktop keeps entries in the encrypted DM store, web command rows private, reply kept, labels accurate.
recent_decisions.why: The worst finding re-granted a withdrawn permission across two devices of one person (holding the self-copy until dm_put_ok meant the other device never learned an untick whose new pass was refused, then minted the defaults). Next worst: the new ring check could drop a call the person allowed because each app reads a stale group list. Fail safe is the rule: a device that did not see the choice never gives back what was withdrawn.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1482.0 (BUG-186): spec 10m merged from both halves and aligned (the web's refused-echo list taken to the desktop; the desktop's withdraw-in-flight-passes-when-marking taken to the web). Plus a leak found while checking: the desktop history pump asked /api/messages?channel=dm:<key> on opening a DM; now only a server's own rooms (net_route::history_channel). Live server checked read-only: 3 nginx lines in the oldest rotated log (ages out within a day), none in the relay journal; nothing deleted.
recent_decisions.why: Multi-device consent must never widen by itself; and the sealed-sender design is undone if the client tells the server whose conversation it opened. Deleting the 3 log lines would be an operator call; they rotate out on their own.

recent_decisions.decision: Spec 10n (commit 91ac73d78): the choice for each friend syncs as its own signed self-note [[hum:choice:v1]]<key>/<may> (newer at wins, equal at: larger may text), the block-notes pattern; passes follow the choice on every device (withdraw beyond at once, echoes never change the choice); 10m R2 withdrawn (self-copies held until dm_put_ok again, refused-echo lists removed); offline Unfollow queued; sweep waits for the mailbox on connect; web scratch pad into the encrypted DM store. Desktop and web built in parallel worktrees.
recent_decisions.why: A third critic, reviewing 10m, found more two-device orderings that lost or reversed a choice (an offline untick undone from the web; a marked friend re-granted with one click; an older echo winning). All share one root: ticks rebuilt from pass echoes that arrive late, out of order or never. Patching orderings one by one does not converge; syncing the choice itself as state, like the block list, does.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1483.0 (BUG-187): spec 10n merged from both halves. The web settled the open details (Unfollow clears as of its signed time, Block regardless; choices survive a server identity change; sweep targets mutual follows and existing pass holders; a tick always succeeds once the store is loaded; contact-request echo under the pass echo rule; 128-bit applied-note hashes) and the desktop matched them. A narrow parity critic ran on the merge.
recent_decisions.why: One spec, two builders, the web going first on details; the parity critic is the last check that both apps reach the same state for the same events.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1483.0 carries 10n + 10o (relay dm_fetch ref echoed on dm_batch; parity fixes) and the operator's evening chat report: image viewer kept above its backdrop (move_to_top), composer grows upward to 45% then scrolls, uploads stream to a part file under a 1 GB route limit with an up-front Content-Length refusal and each person's upload_limit_mb on their own peer-list entry (private conversations stay 6 MB: the receiving side decrypts in memory). nginx change prepared in scripts/nginx/humanity.conf, NOT applied: outward-facing server config, asked the operator. Library A to Z (default) with a Suggested toggle given to an agent. Media showcase drafted as docs/design/files-showcase.md with three open questions.
recent_decisions.why: The operator tested the desktop chat and reported each issue; every fix has a test that reproduced his symptom first (the viewer test found the backdrop layer at screen centre; the upload test reproduced the 400 multipart error with the route layer off). The nginx edge change affects what the public can send to the server, so it waits for his yes even though the relay now refuses oversize uploads itself.

recent_decisions.decision: nginx /api/upload on the VPS changed with the operator's permission ("You have my permission"): client_max_body_size 6m -> 1025m, proxy_request_buffering off, client_body_timeout 300s, proxy send/read timeouts 900s. Backup at /root/humanity.nginx.bak-2026-10-11; nginx -t passed; reloaded; an 8 MB probe now reaches the relay (403 bad token) instead of nginx refusing it. Same change in scripts/nginx/humanity.conf.
recent_decisions.why: The relay now enforces each role's upload limit itself, refusing on the declared size before reading, and streams to a part file; the edge cap of 6 MB had kept every admin upload above 6 MB from reaching it. Applied only after the v0.1483.0 relay was live.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1484.0 (BUG-189): the upload review. Bare ?key= removed from /api/upload, DELETE /api/assets/{id} and the listing-image routes (token only); desktop keeps (server, token) from its own peer-list entry and sends ?token=; web never falls back to the key; Roles can_upload enforced; picture_type by type or extension, 64 MB picture cap, read and strip in spawn_blocking; part files removed on all error paths and at start (clear_part_files); desktop shows the server refusal (upload_error_words); private limit min(6 MB, own). The live nginx upload cap was restored to 6 MB at once (backup of the 1025m version at /root/humanity.nginx.1025m-2026-10-11) and is re-raised after the v0.1484.0 deploy.

recent_decisions.decision: Device-to-device big files: relay, web and desktop halves merged (full verify green, 4034 lib tests). A real two-browser run through a throwaway loopback relay and our forwarder sent 20 MB web to web. The review found: web Sender replaced windows on every get (desktop tops up one piece at a time: 16 min instead of 1 for 2.3 GB), web answerer one transfer per link, desktop dropping early dc_ice while waiting for credentials, desktop receiver allocating 256 KiB for any piece number, file credentials obtainable with a self-signed pass to anyone, and (from the browser run) an answer note refused by a friends-only sender. Rules settled in media-showcase.md (get is additive; one engine per channel; early candidates kept; answer notes carry the file pass, which the relay accepts on dm_put; file credentials need a registered peer, 8 live file allocations a person, refusals counted first). Relay round done; desktop and web fixes dispatched in worktrees. Dev tool: preview-server proxies /ws and binds loopback.
recent_decisions.why: Interop between the two apps had no test (each tested against its own counterpart); a review plus a real browser run found what stand-ins could not.

recent_decisions.decision: Device-to-device second review round. Relay (397ff2750): a dc_offer let in by a file pass is forwarded carrying that pass's id as `file` (relay-set only), so the file's sender asks the forwarder for ONE allocation per connection; a peer signed in without a registered name counts as known; 16 file allocations a person. Rules 7 to 9 written into media-showcase.md (dial names its file; an end is always said, on the channel and by the cancel note; a dial counts as the answer). Web rules 7 to 9 merged (edbbdba69): a sending channel the other side closes is judged after 15 s (connection still up = they stopped it; gone = a drop that waits for the next dial), because ending on any close would break resume after a receiver reload. Desktop BUG-200 merged (387de74c5), then both apps key the 'seen' word by server AND person (a restore from another recovery phrase starts with nothing seen). Real two-browser run through a throwaway relay built from main: fresh-server choice published, refused offer explained, 20 MB via the call relay with the real relay's `file`, 120 MB with the receiver page reloaded mid-transfer resumed to Saved/Sent.
recent_decisions.why: The second review found idle per-offer allocations eating the person's share (and a fifth offer never matching), signed-in placeholder-named peers refused, and silent receiver failures leaving a desktop sender waiting up to 7 days. The 15 s judge is the web agent's call; it is now confirmed in Chromium for the reload case, and the desktop agent was told to match it.

The website can do a limited version only in Chromium browsers (the File System Access API, one folder at a time with permission).
recent_decisions.why: A safe way to publish from a big personal drive: browsing is local, publishing is explicit and per file, and other people's private files on the same drive never move.

recent_decisions.decision: Your folders is DESKTOP ONLY (operator): no website version, so every browser behaves the same and people are drawn to the installed app; the direction he stated: "We have to somehow make HumanityOS better than Steam, GOG, Epic, Brave, Chrome, Safari." New idea, welcomed: a Games library in the app that lists and launches every installed game (Steam, Epic, GOG, and games installed anywhere else, e.g. Dwarf Fortress classic), with the stores still doing downloads, updates and licence checks behind it. Before building: a dated findings doc on Steam's and Epic's terms for listing and launching their games from another app and on what we may not do (download or update their games ourselves); Playnite (open source) is prior art for listing and launching.
recent_decisions.why: One place for a person's games without a store's browser in the way; the store terms decide the line, so they are read from the source first (CLAUDE.md: research a legal question, then write it down and date it).

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1513.0: MP4 (H.264/AAC, and anything else Windows decodes) plays in the desktop player through Windows Media Foundation (src/media/system.rs): media::probe tries our Matroska/AV1 path first, then the system path; the decode thread and kira sound mirror the AV1 path's queue/generation/seek rules. MF's 5 functions are loaded with LoadLibraryW/GetProcAddress, never linked. Each stream counted from Windows's first sample time set to the MP4's declared start (leading empty edits of its edit list; Windows reports video 0.133 s, audio 0.021 s in the fixture where the file says 0). A critic review found and fixed: the real row layout comes only with the first picture (854/1366/portrait H.264 drew skewed), sound that truly starts late, files whose sound Windows cannot decode (sound_lost: converted with ffmpeg on screens, said on the Media page), kira's first seek made the reader on the window thread (now a no-op for a seek to 0), System32-only DLL loading. A new player shows its first picture at once (show_next_frame at open). The Media page's video got sound + Mute (media::sync_sound from the engine's audio frame sync). Card follow-ups closed on both apps.
recent_decisions.why: Operator asked how to play MP4s (2026-10-17) and said to finish the cards and pick the next best work (2026-10-18). Linking mfplat.dll would stop the app starting at all on a Windows N edition, so the functions are loaded at run time and N says the platform finding's sentence. Without the per-stream start, the picture would lag the sound by about 110 ms. Tests that are about our own decoder or the ffmpeg path turn the system decoders off on their thread (system_decoders_off_on_this_thread) because this machine's Windows plays even the VP8 fixture.

recent_decisions.why: The operator asked on 2026-10-18 why HumanityOS takes a long time to start. Leads left: the cloud-noise upload still waits on its bake (0 to 0.8 s); the planet prebuild could start earlier.

recent_decisions.decision: Pipes, cables and similar runs to be laid along splines that snap to surfaces, within real "to code" limits, presented as augmented reality (the HUD layer); a full plan is being written (docs/design/spline-routing.md) before any build.
recent_decisions.why: Operator, verbatim: "We want to make the process of laying pipes, cables, and whatever else as easy as possible. I like the idea of using splines for things with certain \"to code\" things. Like right now all our cables and pipes are just straight tubes and 90 degree corners. With splines we could have curves. I figure this simplified version of interacting with machines, pipes, cables, etc. would be a lot easier for people to digest. We could say it's augmented reality. What we design could literally be used to AR whenever I can afford AR glasses. This is how we can justify the constellation lines we added to the skybox and real star catalog. I guess we would say it's all part of the HUD." Prompted by a post showing a spline mesh deformer with surface snap.

recent_decisions.decision: Spline routing direction, part 2: real-world behaviour first, any run's material changeable, free placement (no grid or voxel cage), runs that function (length, material and route feed the simulation), features slid along a run (sprinkler, tap, drip emitter, tee, valve, junction), anchors including vehicle cable ramps, and tapping into infrastructure as gameplay (hacking an alien craft's data cables, opening a powered door's emergency release panel). Passed to the spline plan agent.
recent_decisions.why: Operator, verbatim: "We should go with what people would experience in the real world. I guess that means we should add a way of changing the material of the pipe/cable/tube/whatever. The spline/line/edge/vertex whatever should be easy to move. I don't want to suffer from fixed voxel placements. I want to see curvy cables/hoses and rigid pipes that area actually doing things instead of just cosmetic. It'd be cool to some how justify a player tapping into infrastructure elements to do things. Like boarding an alien craft, locating their data cables, and then trying to hack in. Like if there's a door and it has emergency panels to remove to manually open powered doors. Players should be able to open that panel. We also want to make adding 'features' to pipes/cables/hoses. Like we have a vertex along the spline we can move to add a water sprinkler for fires or watering plants or whatever." And: "The we could add the ability to add anchors or remove anchors to keep cables/hoses/whatever anchored with like those ramps so they can be driven over safely with heavy machinery/vehicals."

Coordinator audit from the code (not memory): NO anti-aliasing of any kind (billboard_bake.rs: "this engine has no MSAA anywhere"; no TAA, no motion vectors, no upscaling or render scale); no local-light shadows (shadows agent running); no specular reflections indoors (no SSR, no reflection probes; room probes carry irradiance only); no skin subsurface scattering, cloth sheen or clearcoat; no decals; light intensity is a multiplier, not photometric units; no HDR display output; no parallax/displacement; no DOF or motion blur; characters' eyes and teeth not converted. Present: sun shadows with cascades, bloom, exposure, AO, bounced room light, atmosphere, clouds, light shafts, ocean, particles. Plan: after the shadows agent, one agent writes the whole renderer gap plan (each gap's 2030 technique, budget on the RTX 4070 and an RX 580-class card, its Settings control with a cost line, build order; anti-aliasing with motion vectors likely first, as upscaling, hair and foliage stability depend on it); the building waits for the weekly reset (2026-11-13 03:00 UTC).

recent_decisions.why: Determinism makes the whole piece knowable, which is what long-range musical structure needs.

recent_decisions.decision: Owner branch SECOND REVIEW: not merged. Both critics agree nobody takes the owner role without the code or the owner key and earlier findings 1,3,4,7-10 are fixed at root, but the two-phase re-seal is structurally weak: the acceptance digest is computable from plaintext hashes without opening anything (owner-alone garbage swap on successor removal), the recipient check is an unlogged read of every copy by a non-owner, change grants let the owner read without an export, every change hands the relay the restore keys (whole manifest), and the recipient identity is the relay's word (a compromised relay lists its own key as "Bea"). MY CALL: held seal v4, a change RE-WRAPS part keys and never re-encrypts bodies (header key commitment; pieces bind the commitment not the slot list; the relay keeps bodies byte for byte and checks the commitment; recipients check only their own slot; no restore keys move; acceptance over the staged header hashes + round id), plus fingerprint/pinned-key recipient choice, rollback/carry-out exclusion, held-caller domain line, /claim near misses, reload/socket, owner-key link redeem refused, bounded ClaimMisses. Brief wk-ownerfix3.txt. ALSO a LIVE bug on main found by the web critic: signed requests sign purpose+ts exactly like chat messages, so posting the chat line account_export hands the room a 5-minute replayable credential for POST /api/account/export; brief wk-sigreq.txt (domain line + one-time nonce for every non-chat signed request). The second release today goes WITHOUT the owner work (APK + whatever lands from pagesfirst/music2); owner ships after a third review.
recent_decisions.why: Envelope encryption (re-wrap the data key) is the standard design for changing recipients; it removes the content exposure the check created instead of patching around it. The operator: We just want to make sure the system itself cannot be abused.

2026-11-12 (operator): "How would you do muscles with math? A line that kind of swells to a sphere. Bigger muscles = more lines? or just 1 scales up some how?" Proposal sent: a spindle muscle is one curve from origin to insertion with a swelling radius profile; a broad muscle (chest, back) is a fan of several curves; size is cross-section (strength follows cross-sectional area), not more curves; contraction keeps volume (shorter and thicker), driving the skin's bulge when flexing (character-animation.md rungs 8 and 9). And: "Can basalt fibre safely be used for casual, formal, recreational clothing?" (answered: protective gear only, itchy and brittle for everyday wear; everyday cloth from flax, hemp, cotton and wool; the research pass confirms).
